instruction: How will the peak intensity and half width of the 12.6 ° characteristic peak of additives added to perovskite precursors to prepare thin films change in XRD characterization?
input: "control": "The combined treatment featured a PCE of 16.72%, FF of 65.57%, Voc of 1.06 V, and Jsc of 24.08 mA/cm². The perovskite solution (1.73 mol/L) was prepared according to chemical formula of Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1. Different concentrations of Me-2PACz were added into the perovskite precursor solution for modification. The incorporation of PEABr (0.8 mg/mL) additive was ensured. The perovskite layer was deposited via a two-step spin-coating procedure with 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. In the last 6 s of the second step, the anti-solvent (160 µL of chlorobenzene) was dropped in the center at a constant rate within 1 s. The samples were subsequently annealed on a hotplate at 110 °C for 25 min. XRD analysis showed a diffraction peak was identified at around 12.65°, with an intensity of 1327.548021 cts and a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 0.188840712, which corresponds to the characteristic peak of PbI2. The relatively low intensity of this peak suggests a limited presence of residual PbI2.", "target": "The PSC device gives the highest PCE of 18.2%, with VOC of 1.1 V, JSC of 22.87 mA/cm², and FF of 72.67%. Perovskite precursor solution (1.73 mol/L) was prepared based on the stoichiometric ratio of Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1. The SAM material Me-4PACz (0.33 mg/mL) was subsequently added into the perovskite solution to enhance interfacial properties and optimize device performance. The addition of PEABr (0.5 mg/mL) as an additive was carefully prepared. The film was deposited under controlled conditions, involving an initial spin of 1000 rpm (10 s) followed by a second spin at 5000 rpm (30 s). A 160 µL CB was dropped onto the substrate at the last 6 s of the spin-coating, resulting in the formation of dark brown films. After spin-coating, the films were annealed on the hot plate at 110 °C for 25 min. XRD analysis showed a diffraction peak was identified at around 12.65°, with an intensity of 789.6191091 cts and a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 0.202154677, which corresponds to the characteristic peak of PbI2. The relatively low intensity of this peak suggests a limited presence of residual PbI2."
